title: Architecture Models and Securing Infrastructure

header.html: 3.1 Compare and contrast security implications of different architecture models; 3.2 Given a scenario, manage the security architecture to best protect the infrastructure
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Architecture and infrastructure models

Model Meaning Security point
Cloud Rented computing from a provider Shared responsibility: the provider secures the platform, you secure data, identities and configuration
Serverless Code runs without managing servers Less to patch, but permissions and code still matter
Multicloud Using more than one cloud provider Avoids lock-in, adds complexity and more places to secure
Deployment models Public, private, hybrid (mix), community (shared by a group with common needs) More control in private, more flexibility in public
Infrastructure as code (IaC) Infrastructure defined in files Repeatable and reviewable; scan the code for mistakes
Operational technology (OT) Industrial control systems Long life, hard to patch: segment it
On-premises Your own datacenter Full control, you carry all the cost and responsibility
Air-gapped network No connection to other networks Strongest isolation; still at risk from removable media and insiders
Microservices An app split into small services Smaller blast radius, but many APIs to secure
Segmentation Logical (VLANs, subnets) or physical (separate hardware) Limits lateral movement

Considerations when choosing

Technical Business
Availability, resilience, proprietary vs open source, usability, responsibility, compute, power requirements, ease of recovery Data sovereignty (laws of the data's location), data classification, cost, ownership, environmental requirements, scalability, risk
Exam tip

. In the cloud, you always keep responsibility for your data, identities and configuration. Data sovereignty = the country's laws apply to the data stored there. An air gap is isolation, not immunity.

2Protecting the infrastructure

Topic Key ideas
Device placement Put devices where they control traffic: firewall at the edge, sensors at choke points
Security zones Group systems by trust: internal, DMZ (screened subnet for public servers), untrusted (internet), guest
Attack surface Reduce it: close ports, remove services, limit exposure
Diversity Use different vendors, platforms and controls so one flaw does not break everything
Failure modes Fail open (stays available when it fails) vs fail closed (blocks when it fails: secure but can stop business)

Zero Trust architecture

Zero Trust removes implicit trust. Elements in the objectives:

  • User authentication: strong, continuous verification.
  • Device management: device health (is it patched and compliant?) and inventory.
  • Application access control: access to each application, not the whole network.
  • Control plane vs data plane: policy decisions are made in the control plane and enforced in the data plane. Beyond the objectives

Secure communication and access

Item Purpose
VPN, remote access, tunneling Encrypted paths for remote users and sites
User management and least privilege Only the needed access
End-to-end encrypted messaging Only the sender and receiver can read
Out-of-band management Manage devices over a separate, protected path
File transfer Use secure protocols (SFTP, FTPS) instead of plain FTP
Security Service Edge (SSE) Cloud-delivered security (web gateway, ZTNA, cloud access broker) for users anywhere

Identity management

Group managed service accounts (gMSAs) give services automatically managed passwords. Use least privilege access accounts. Watch privilege creep: users collecting rights as they change roles.

Exam tip

. A screened subnet (DMZ) holds public-facing servers between two firewalls. Fail closed protects security; fail open protects availability (for example a fire exit door). Privilege creep is solved by access reviews.

Exam tip

. Segmentation limits lateral movement, and Zero Trust removes trust based on location: both reduce the blast radius of a breach.

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors hosts its public web servers in a separate network between two firewalls. What is this network called?

  • AAir-gapped network
  • BOut-of-band network
  • CScreened subnet (DMZ)
  • DCommunity cloud
Show the answer

Answer: C. A screened subnet or DMZ holds public-facing servers, separated from the internal network.

S2A factory control network must have no connection to any other network. Which design fits?

  • AAir-gapped network
  • BHybrid cloud
  • CMulticloud
  • DServerless
Show the answer

Answer: A. An air-gapped network has no connection to other networks.

S3A company stores customer data in a cloud region in another country and worries about local laws. Which concept applies?

  • AData masking
  • BFailover testing
  • CData sovereignty
  • DPrivilege creep
Show the answer

Answer: C. Data sovereignty means the data is subject to the laws of the country where it is stored.

S4A door controller fails and the door locks everyone out to protect the room. Which failure mode is this?

  • AFail open
  • BFail forward
  • CFail closed
  • DFail over
Show the answer

Answer: C. The system defaults to a secure, blocking state, which is fail closed.

S5Administrators manage network switches over a dedicated protected network separate from production traffic. What is this called?

  • ATunneling
  • BOut-of-band management
  • CSegmentation by VLAN
  • DWireless intrusion prevention
Show the answer

Answer: B. Managing devices over a separate path from the data network is out-of-band management.

S6Users move between teams and keep all their old permissions. Which problem is this?

  • APrivilege creep
  • BData sovereignty
  • CDiversity
  • DFailover
Show the answer

Answer: A. Accumulating permissions as roles change is privilege creep.

3.2 Recall questions

R1Name the four cloud deployment models.

Show the answer

Public, private, hybrid and community.

R2What does IaC stand for?

Show the answer

Infrastructure as code.

R3What is the purpose of segmentation?

Show the answer

To limit lateral movement and contain damage.

R4What is the difference between fail open and fail closed?

Show the answer

Fail open stays available when it fails; fail closed blocks to stay secure.

R5What does SSE provide?

Show the answer

Cloud-delivered security services such as a web gateway and Zero Trust network access.

R6What is a gMSA?

Show the answer

A group managed service account with automatically managed passwords.

4Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Models cloud (shared responsibility), serverless, multicloud, public/private/hybrid/community, IaC, OT, on-premises, air-gapped, microservices
Choosing availability, resilience, usability, ease of recovery; data sovereignty, classification, cost, scalability, risk
Protect device placement, security zones (DMZ), reduce attack surface, diversity, fail open vs closed
Zero Trust verify users and devices (health, inventory), per-application access
Access VPN, tunneling, E2E messaging, out-of-band management, secure file transfer, SSE; gMSAs, least privilege, watch privilege creep
